ai.description: *Cnemaspis mahabali* is a small gecko reaching 34 mm SVL. It features a brownish-grey dorsum with a distinct yellow vertebral stripe and a row of small, pale tubercles along its flanks.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cnemaspis mahabali* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, bright yellow or orange patch on its throat, which is absent in other similar Western Ghats species.
ai.habitat: *Cnemaspis mahabali* is endemic to the Western Ghats, typically inhabiting moist deciduous and evergreen forests at elevations between 200 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: Cnemaspis mahabali is a diurnal gecko that actively forages for small insects on rock surfaces and tree trunks during the bright daylight hours.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis mahabali* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two spherical eggs. Breeding occurs throughout the year, with peak activity observed during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cnemaspis mahabali* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala, India, where it inhabits low-to-mid elevation rocky habitats.
